root_cause.text: The nf_tables netdev event handlers incorrectly treated existing hook ops as a duplicate only during device rename (`changename && ops`), so on `NETDEV_REGISTER` they could add a second `nf_hook_ops` for a device already registered by `nft_netdev_hook_alloc()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the `NETDEV_REGISTER` guard in both `nft_flowtable_event()` and `nft_netdev_event()` from `if (!match || (changename && ops))` to `if (!match || ops)`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states duplicate registration must be avoided because the device may already have been added by `nft_netdev_hook_alloc()` when creating the hook.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid re-registering flowtable hook operations on NETDEV_REGISTER when they are already present.
intent_record.what: In the NETDEV_REGISTER case of nft_flowtable_event(), the condition guarding the continue statement was changed from `if (!match || (changename && ops))` to `if (!match || ops)`.
intent_record.how: This makes the handler skip registration whenever matching hook operations already exist, regardless of whether the event is a name change, preventing duplicate or unnecessary allocation/registration on NETDEV_REGISTER events.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent duplicate netdev base chain registration on NETDEV_REGISTER by always skipping devices that already have ops.
intent_record.what: In the NETDEV_REGISTER case of nft_netdev_event(), the conditional `if (!match || (changename && ops))` was changed to `if (!match || ops)`, removing the dependency on `changename` when deciding to skip processing for an already registered ops entry.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this causes the handler to always skip registration when a matching device already has an associated `ops` object, instead of only skipping in rename-related cases. This prevents duplicate registration or re-creation of ops for already registered devices during NETDEV_REGISTER events.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent duplicate netdev base chain registration on NETDEV_REGISTER by always skipping devices that already have ops.

consistency_review.core_intent: Prevent duplicate registration of existing netdevice flowtable/base-chain hook operations during NETDEV_REGISTER events.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly fix the root cause by preventing duplicate nf_hook_ops registration on NETDEV_REGISTER for existing flowtable and base-chain netdevice hooks, removing the incorrect changename-only duplicate check.

candidates.rationale: This conditional is the root cause: it treats existing hook ops as a duplicate only when changename is true. On NETDEV_REGISTER, an already existing ops does not cause skipping unless renaming, allowing duplicate nf_hook_ops registration.

This identical condition in the base-chain netdev event handler incorrectly skips already-registered devices only for rename events. During NETDEV_REGISTER it fails to reject existing ops, leading to duplicate hook registration.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition only treats existing hook ops as a reason to skip when changename is true. On NETDEV_REGISTER, ops can already exist from nft_netdev_hook_alloc(), but this statement does not reject that case, allowing duplicate nf_hook_ops registration.

This identical conditional in the netdev base-chain event handler has the same flaw: existing ops are ignored unless the event is a rename. As a result, NETDEV_REGISTER can proceed with an already registered device and add duplicate hook operations.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact NETDEV_REGISTER/UNREGISTER handling and the duplicate-registration guard. The vulnerable construct is present in `nft_flowtable_event()`: in the `NETDEV_REGISTER` case it uses `if (!match || (changename && ops)) continue;`. This means an existing `ops` only prevents registration when `changename` is true. For ordinary `NETDEV_REGISTER` events (`changename == false`), even if `ops` already exists, the code does not skip and proceeds to allocate/register another hook via `ops = kzalloc(...)` and `nf_register_net_hook(...)`. That matches the root cause: existing hook ops are treated as duplicate only during rename, not during regular register. The fix would require skipping registration whenever `ops` already exists, i.e. logic equivalent to `if (!match || ops) continue;`, but that is not what this code does. The commit message itself even notes: `this patch also skips for NETDEV_REGISTER if the device is already registered`, but the actual code only checks `(changename && ops)`, so the complete fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the full newly added NETDEV_REGISTER handling in the relevant event path. The root cause is failure to treat an existing hook ops as a duplicate on register events, allowing a second nf_hook_ops to be added for a device already registered by nft_netdev_hook_alloc(). In this commit, the new NETDEV_REGISTER case in nft_flowtable_event() does exactly that: after matching the interface name with `if (strcmp(hook->ifname, dev->name)) continue;`, it unconditionally allocates a new hook op via `ops = kzalloc(sizeof(struct nf_hook_ops), GFP_KERNEL_ACCOUNT);`, initializes it, calls `nft_register_flowtable_ops(...)`, and then appends it with `list_add_tail_rcu(&ops->list, &hook->ops_list);`. bic_trace_step.reason: The provided code is sufficient because it contains the entire flowtable netdev event handling introduced by this commit. The vulnerability root cause refers to netdev event handlers that wrongly considered duplicates only under a condition like `changename && ops`, allowing duplicate `nf_hook_ops` insertion on `NETDEV_REGISTER`. In this commit's flowtable code, that logic is not present at all. The notifier path is limited to unregister handling only: `if (event != NETDEV_UNREGISTER) return 0;` in `nf_tables_flowtable_event()`, and the per-flowtable handler only unregisters and nulls an existing hook: `nf_unregister_net_hook(dev_net(dev), &flowtable->ops[i]); flowtable->ops[i].dev = NULL;`. There is no handling for `NETDEV_REGISTER`, no rename handling, and no duplicate-check condition involving `changename && ops`. Hook registration for flowtables happens only at creation time in `nf_tables_newflowtable()` via `for (i = 0; i < flowtable->ops_len; i++) { err = nf_register_net_hook(net, &flowtable->ops[i]); ... }`. Therefore the specific vulnerable construct described in the root cause is absent from this function set in this commit. At the same time, the eventual fix described by the root cause is also not present, because there is no broader duplicate-detection logic for register/rename events here.
